problem_type: MCP model integration had a completed protocol probe with no production caller
symptom: A user giving an MCP host a relay URL and saved key still had to guess model IDs and model types, so connected models could be unusable without an explanation.
direct_cause: nomi_integration.propose required agent-supplied candidates and never called ConnectionCertificationService.discoverHttpModels; the list parser also discarded OpenRouter architecture metadata.
class_root: The deterministic /models discovery contract was owned by onboarding code but had no shared MCP session boundary consuming it, leaving candidate identity and capability derivation to a second, less reliable author.
affected_population: Signed MCP hosts connecting OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic relays
Bare /models responses containing only model IDs
OpenRouter-style model records with architecture metadata
Relays that do not expose /models or /v1/models
internal_only_reason: This remediation enforces an internal Nomi routing invariant over the already-tested model-list protocol; no third-party contract decision is required.
invariants: MCP HTTP integration proposal discovery uses the main-process credential resolver and the canonical discoverHttpModels boundary.
OpenRouter architecture modalities are preserved through parsing and derive candidate modes without vendor-specific branches.
A bare unmatched model ID is explicitly classified as an unknown plain-text candidate with a human repair instruction.
A missing model-list route fails closed with a human instruction to enter model IDs manually and never claims discovery success.
generality_proof: All MCP HTTP integrations converge on IntegrationSessionService.propose, while all model-list callers share modelListResponse/modelListProbe. Preserving optional descriptors at that parser boundary and deriving candidates in the session boundary covers rich and bare responses without provider branches or credential values crossing MCP.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own MCP discovery timing, credential resolution, candidate persistence, and human fallback errors.
Normalize model IDs and preserve optional architecture metadata for every list protocol.
Convert canonical list results into generic capability candidates using declared metadata, catalog matches, or explicit plain-text fallback.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Dispatcher routes the MCP action to IntegrationSessionService.propose, the shared discovery boundary.
The UI path already consumes fetchModelList; parser metadata is additive and preserves its existing string-model result contract.
This path compiles media request mappings after candidate selection; it is retained for parameter and wire-shape certification, not MCP model-list discovery.

recurrence.reason: Any new MCP relay could reproduce the zero-caller gap or lose capability metadata when its /models shape changes.
same_class_scan: rg discoverHttpModels across electron and tests found only the service wrapper before this change.
rg fetchModelList callers confirmed onboarding IPC and vendor health are separate consumers of the same probe.
rg docsDiscovery/compiler confirmed the certification compiler remains a distinct media-shape path and is not an equivalent candidate-list owner.

prevention.invariant: An MCP HTTP proposal without agent candidates performs canonical discovery with a main-process-resolved credential before persisting candidates.
prevention.failure_mode: Discovery errors are converted to a readable missing-route/auth/network instruction that offers manual model ID entry; no secret or false success is returned.
prevention.strategy: Make the session state machine, rather than the driving model, the only owner of MCP candidate discovery and capability fallback.

legacy_paths.rationale: The old providerAdapter docsDiscovery/compiler path cannot be deleted in this scoped change because certification still needs it for non-text parameter and wire-shape compilation. It is not used for MCP candidate discovery; retaining it is an explicit bounded dependency rather than a second MCP discovery path.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the invariant; the change uses existing fetch and parser code.

migration: No persisted schema changes. Existing sessions with agent-provided candidates continue through the original proposal path; sessions that omit candidates now discover at propose time.
residual_risks: OpenRouter metadata can declare modalities but cannot prove request wire shape; canonical certification still performs the real minimum production request.
ProviderAdapter documentation compilation remains a separate certification concern and is intentionally retained for media models.
